findings.claim: Idle-subtracted CPU package energy per batch of the common Gaussian VI workload (NumPy float64 reference)

hypothesis: The deterministic work of a fixed-step RK4 geodesic trajectory is exactly 4N right-hand-side evaluations, and that of a batch of the common Gaussian VI workload exactly replicas x (24 K + 7) operations; their CPU energy can be read only from package counters bracketing repeated batches, which an operator captures outside the lab runner.
input_data: 6 unit-speed geodesics on the unit sphere from the equator, headings [0.7, 0.85, 1.0, 1.15, 1.3, 1.45] rad, length 3.0
the common Gaussian VI workload (examples/energy-accuracy/problem.json, K = 38 iterations, 4096 replicas, NumPy float64 reference of the gaussian_vi PTX kernel)
optional operator capture bound as rapl-log (--capture rapl-log=PATH or CIW_LAB_RAPL_LOG)
mathematical_model: E_gross = sum over package domains of (E(after) - E(before)) / units, one wrap allowed; E_idle-subtracted = (E_gross_total - E_idle * t_work / t_idle) / units, where units are trajectories (repeats x 6) or common-workload batches; work proxy W = 4N evaluations (RK4), the Dormand-Prince count, or replicas x (24 K + 7) flops for a Gaussian VI batch.
numerical_result: 1024 evaluations per RK4 trajectory; max endpoint error 1.09e-09; adaptive evaluations [487, 427, 361, 337, 313, 295]; 3764224 flops per common-workload batch; energy: not measured (no accepted RAPL capture; the runner acquires no energy measurement)
observation_model: Evaluations counted by wrapping Surface.geodesic_rhs; Gaussian VI operations counted by instrumenting the NumPy reference and compared with the kernel's PTX instructions; a supplied capture is read-only input whose raw bytes are retained; the hardware:rapl probe (only with a capture) reads one counter value to confirm readability and discards it; wall/CPU time retained only as an artifact.

title: Measure CPU energy per geodesic trajectory.
uncertainty: Work counts are exact; a RAPL energy would carry model error, background load and a model-dependent counter unit (commonly 2^-16 J), none characterized here.
unresolved_assumptions: Evaluation and operation counts are work proxies, not energy measurements
Package energy is not attributed to this process; idle subtraction assumes the idle interval after the workload represents the background during it
A capture is an operator record: identity binding is checked, authenticity is not

CPU energy per common-workload batch (here) and GPU energy per batch (T116) are for the same computation (the RAPL gate and T116's NVML gate both require the common workload's kernel, problem, prepared inputs, K and replicas) but different counters, scopes and batch boundaries: package versus whole device; the NumPy bracket excludes the prepared inputs (computed once before bracketing) and includes their per-batch broadcast to the replica columns, the GPU batch includes launch, synchronization, copy and the worker's output check; no finding combines them
